claims.text: Manual 3D medical image segmentation is time-consuming, while task-specific expert models require data curation and engineering expertise; rare pathologies and animal data also motivate zero-shot segmentation and interactive correction.
VISTA3D unifies automatic segmentation for 127 supported classes, interactive editing, and 3D point-prompted zero-shot segmentation through two branches sharing an image encoder.

The model uses a MONAI SegResNet CNN backbone, 128-voxel cubic training patches, and sliding-window inference. Its automatic head accepts a class index and produces a binary segmentation; its interactive head accepts positive and negative 3D clicks.

Interactive refinement merges the independent branch outputs by adding or removing only connected-component regions containing the relevant clicks, aiming to avoid unintended changes to correct segmentation regions.

The curated dataset contains 11,454 CT volumes from in-house and public sources. Each source is randomly split into 64% training, 16% validation, and 20% test data; TotalSegmentator supplies 117-class pseudo-labels and SAM supplies supervoxels for every scan, with unreliable pseudo-labels removed by post-processing.

The proposed supervoxel method sums upsampled SAM ViT-H features extracted in axial, coronal, and sagittal views, then applies SLIC with nsegments = 100 and sigma = 3. These supervoxels train the interactive branch to transfer SAM knowledge to 3D segmentation.

Training proceeds through interactive-branch training, interactive finetuning with dataset oversampling, automatic-branch training with the encoder frozen, and automatic finetuning using MAISI-generated anomalies to augment under-represented classes.

Across the 14 datasets in Table 1, average Dice scores are 0.706 for Auto3DSeg, 0.718 for nnUNet, 0.711 for VISTA3D automatic segmentation, 0.760 for VISTA3D point segmentation, and 0.792 for VISTA3D automatic segmentation with point correction.

In the supported-class evaluation, a 'single point' means one click per sliding-window patch, and a click affects only the 128-voxel cubic patch containing it; correction clicks are simulated from false-positive or false-negative regions.
TotalSegV2 comparisons are biased toward nnUNet and TotalSegmentator because the ground truth was generated by pretrained TotalSegmentator, and its training data may include the study's test split.

Zero-shot evaluation uses four external datasets: 140 mouse micro-CT scans at 0.2 mm resolution with four annotated organs, 210 C4KC-KITS kidney-tumor scans, 53 adrenocortical-carcinoma scans, and 105 hepatocellular-carcinoma scans.

The authors report superior zero-shot accuracy with reduced annotation effort and report that removing supervoxel training worsens zero-shot performance; the supplied figure text does not provide numerical Dice curves.

On a 16 GB V100 GPU, a 512 × 512 × 512 volume resampled to 1.5 mm isotropic spacing takes 2m09s for VISTA3D's default 118-class segmentation versus 12m01s for TotalSegmentator's default 117-class segmentation, without special model optimization.

With one training case, VISTA3D achieves held-out average Dice scores of 0.926 on mouse micro-CT and 0.795 on WORD, compared with 0.820/0.214 for Auto3DSeg, 0.759/0.185 for nnU-Net, and 0.791/0.779 for TotalSegmentator. At 100 WORD training cases, VISTA3D and TotalSegmentator both score 0.875.
Extending support to MRI and PET, improving zero-shot interaction, and validating and integrating the workflow with clinical partners are identified as future work.
